utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Bring in the witness, please. Good morning to the interpreters, good morning to everyone. Does everybody hear me? We can now continue, that is, as soon as the witness is in the courtroom, of course. (The witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: General, do you hear me? Do you hear me, Brigadier?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, I think we're getting some overlap in the interpretation booth. I am getting the Croatian translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Do you hear me in English?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, I hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Do you hear my voice, there?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I hear you, but I also hear Maya.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Are you getting the English? Do you hear me Brigadier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not getting the Croatian translation. I am not getting the Croatian translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Registrar, do you think we should suspend --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: It's fine now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Did you have a restful night, Brigadier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Today is going to be long. Mr. Kehoe is going to continue with the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours, Counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Kehoe:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Brigadier.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, we are again moving into another subject area here, and one of the areas that you discussed, and this was in your arguments or in your statements in response to Defence's questions concerning the problems of command in Central Bosnia. You noted that Colonel Blaskic couldn't appoint and dismiss brigade commanders and other commanders, except with the input and approval of the locals, the local municipal authorities. And specifically, if we could just go through your transcript of your prior testimony on direct. On page 12.170, you noted at line 9 that if you want to appoint a brigade commander, before doing anything else, the commander of the Operative Zone, Colonel Blaskic, had to reach an agreement with municipal authorities. When such an agreement was reached, information from the commander would be submitted through the brigade commander to the commander of the Operative Zone to the highest level and to the president of the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna. On page 12.072, you noted that the method in appointing of commanders, a major influence and a decisive role was played by the municipal functionaries; if we are talking about the commanders, at the municipal level. Lastly, on page 12.147 you again noted on line 12 that with regard to appointments of brigade commanders the key role was played by the local political authorities with respect to the brigades and with respect to the subordinate units. We discussed, or Defence put several documents in, one particular document we will talk about briefly, which prompted a question from Judge Riad which said, Judge Riad asked, "So, this is not stated at all in these documents, the practice was contrary to the orders."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman is not satisfied by this long introduction, and he is wondering whether you are arguing or whether your making a final statement. He doesn't really understand the question you're going to ask, nor have the Judges understood. Mr. Kehoe, we don't really have a great deal of time, try to go right to the questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I am, Judge. I'm just going back to -- the questions are going to be based on what the witness said in the past, and we're merely going to it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is my final point. The question was, "How did you dismiss a commander? Was the permission of the municipal authorities required for this, too, or could the Commander in Chief do so directly?" And your answer was, "The approval was required of the municipal authorities." So, your point, sir, was that the municipal authorities were both, the approval of those authorities was needed to both dismiss and appoint commanders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We understood that, Mr. Kehoe. Let's go forward, come on. We've already understood that. Now take the documents out and ask the questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us turn our attention to two documents, sir, Defence Exhibit 47, and, Mr. Dubuisson, the excerpts from the Narodni Lists, which I believe is Defence Exhibit 38, if we could just go to the area that's tabbed. We're going to deal with the articles in that tab right there, which is article 29 and 34, on the tabbed page, sir. Defence Exhibit 247, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Was that 47 or 247? I didn't quite get the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: 247, Mr. President. Defence 247. If we could put the ELMO on in the video booth, please. Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, do you have those documents before you, both the Narodni Lists, Articles 29 and 34?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As well as Defence Exhibit 247?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have both documents in front of me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's move through these quickly, Brigadier. Starting on Article 29, correct me if I'm wrong, but the article, and we will move straight to the pertinent part in Article 29, where it says: "The supreme commander of the armed forces of the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna shall be the president of the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna presidency. The supreme commander shall appoint and dismiss from duty military commanders in accordance with the special provision." Now, let us turn our attention to Article 34, and we will be focusing on subdivision 2 in that article. Article 34, "Commanders in the armed forces shall be appointed and dismissed as follows: The presidency of the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna shall appoint and dismiss commanders of brigades and high ranking officers. The Croatian Defence Council, HVO, shall appoint and dismiss commanders of battalions and companies, as well as other officers; and brigade commanders shall appoint and dismiss commanders of platoons, detachments and other non-commissioned officers." Now, let us turn our attention to Defence Exhibit 34, where there is apparently a request for clarification on the power to appoint and dismiss. And Blaskic answers that, and I believe during the Defence direct you identified this document as Colonel Blaskic's signature. The accused calls on Article 34 in this document, and let me read it and move to the pertinent part on number 2. "Further, to the provisions of Article 34 of the decree of the armed forces of the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna," and he refers to the Narodni List Gazette, the Official Gazette, "the order of the main HVO headquarters 396, of 27 June 1992, and the authorisation of the head of the Defence office of the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna, 0323992, of 4 December 1992, we hereby give you some clarification on the persons authorised to appoint officers and non-commissioned officers to certain posts and to dismiss them and the procedure for this." Let's move to 2. "The head of the Defence office and the commanders authorised by him appoint and dismiss other officers, i.e. persons who have been proposed for these officer posts. Now, do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Blaskic was given an authorisation by the head of the defence officers to appoint and dismiss; wasn't he, pursuant to Article 34?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: General Blaskic had the authority, the prescribed authority envisaged by procedure to appoint and dismiss commanders in the way envisaged by the provisions of Article 34 of the decree that we have before you, that is, on the basis of the authorisation he was given. I'm not sure whether he was given that authorisation by the president of the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna or the head of the defence department. This can be seen from the documents on commander appointments. It was on the basis of that authorisation that he appointed the commanders within the scope of competence of the president of the presidency. That is those above the level of the Operative Zone. Why General Blaskic was given such authorisation was, in my personal opinion, the fact that we were cut off and that we were unable to communicate with our superiors, and to ensure greater efficiency of operations. That was the rule. But in practice, things were different. On the basis of this article, General Blaskic wrote appointments and dismissals; but for that to be carried out, for the document that he wrote to be implemented, he had to have the approval and had to have consultations, both in the case of appointments and dismissals. Sometimes we had commanders of municipal headquarters, sometimes brigade commanders, in those cases he had to have the approval of political representatives. That is, representatives of the civilian municipal authorities. Because, throughout the war, during the paralysis of the authorities of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the municipalities functioned as a state. When talking about lower level appointments of platoon or company commanders, which the brigade commander was authorised to do, the brigade commander could not carry out that appointment in a village, the commander of a platoon or a company, if the village did not approve of that commander, because such a person would have no authority at all. That was the reality. What we are talking about are the provisions, the regulated provisions based on the decree of the armed forces of Herceg-Bosna and Article 34, which authorised General Blaskic to do this. And he did so, but under the conditions I've described, both when it had to do with appointments and dismissals. I think that we have several such orders here that have been tendered by the Defence, as far as I recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, this document has been tendered by the Defence, Brigadier, and nothing of what you said appears in this document, does it, where Blaskic himself is issuing a clarification on the appointment to, on the authorisation to appoint and dismiss; none of what you said is in this clarification.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: General Blaskic, in this document, provides clarifications for brigade commanders. I assume this clarification was necessary, because in the brigade command they probably didn't have this decree on the armed forces, so that the provisions of that decree have been copied so that the brigades would know what was meant. Because it can be seen that the supreme commander can transfer his authority to a commander. The procedure was as I have described, and as corroborated by the documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's turn to some of those documents, and with the assistance of the usher, we will move through some documents relatively quickly. And if we can gather them at once, 456/62, 456/ --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Are you still talking about the same subject?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Still the same subject, Judge. We have a few more questions, we're going to move through quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The Judges really do understand the difference in the point of view here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I understand, Judge, but we have some documents to explore this area, in light of some of the issues that have been raised, that possibly will clarify the issue a little more. Again, Mr. Dubuisson, it's 456/62, 456/63, 456/64, 456/65, 456/66 and 456/67. That would be 456/62 through 456/67, in series. I assure you, Mr. President, we will move through these documents quickly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the first document, Brigadier, do you see that document? It's dated, actually it's dated the 4th of July 1992. At least that's the stamp in the upper left-hand corner of the document.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: It is a document 95/14, is that the document you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, it's not. If I can take a look, it should be Exhibit 456/62, and the stamp on the upper left-hand corner is 4 July 1992.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: The document I have in my hand is marked IT-95-14-T. That's the document that I have -- but the number doesn't fit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, this is a document signed by Colonel Blaskic; is it not?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Could we please check whether we're talking about the same document? Or could you please read the first sentence so I know I have the right document? The document I have in my hand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It says, "Bearing in mind the need to form zones of responsibility or operative zones, in the region of Central Bosnia, I hereby issue the following."

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that document signed by Colonel Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, this is General Blaskic's signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Is that his stamp?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is the stamp of the regional headquarters for Central Bosnia, this headquarters was operating with a base in Gornji Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this document on the 4th of July 1992, Blaskic is appointing four commanders for four Operative Zones throughout the Central Bosnia Operative Zone; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the first paragraph that is what it says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, is it your testimony that Blaskic consulted with all the municipal leaders when he appointed these Operative Zone commanders, before he appointed them?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: I claim with respect to this document, as follows: Even though I was not in this headquarters at the time, but I know what the practice was for the general to appoint these people, and when I was speaking about the organisation I said that there were regional crisis staffs with representatives of the political authorities in the municipality on them; and for such a document to be passed, and for such appointments to be made, General Blaskic had to act in this way. Especially as General Blaskic didn't even know these people at the time, because he was serving in Slovenia, and he certainly had to have consultations and get the green light to appoint such people. This was particularly pronounced at the beginning when people were suspicious about certain commanders and didn't trust them, and the people demanded, and the politicians insisted that those people should be appointed which the people felt would lead them best in the struggle and who would best organise defence in their area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's turn to the next document, the 24th of October 1992, which is 456/63. Now, this is a document, is it signed by Colonel Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, this document was signed by General Blaskic. This is his signature of the command of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone headquarters. This can be seen from the stamp, that was how it was called at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this document, Blaskic is nominating Colonel Filip Filipovic commander of the municipal headquarters in Travnik and Nikola Grubic deputy commander. Now, prior to doing this, is it your testimony that he had to consult with the municipal authorities in order to appoint these people?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: He certainly had to consult with those authorities, and it can be seen from this order that the commander wrote this order on the basis of the authorisation he was given by the main headquarters, the authorisation I explained a moment ago; and especially in this case he had to have consultations with representatives of the municipal authorities, because Filipovic had only just arrived from the former Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's turn our attention to 456/64, which is an order of Blaskic on the 20th of November 1992. Now, in this particular document, again, this is a packet communication; is it not?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, a packet communication.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this document Blaskic says: "In view of the situation on the front, I hereby appoint a new defence sector commander and relieve the present commander of his duties. 1. Mr. Ivica Rajic being appointed commander of section one, and Mr. Ivica Cosic deputy commander,. 2. Mr. Zivko Tojic shall be appointed commander of sector Two, and Mario Cerkez" -- it probably was Mario Cerkez, and it says that in the original -- "deputy commander." Now, in this particular document, Blaskic is both appointing and relieving commanders, at least that's what the preparatory language is?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't see anyone here. Yes, I see, that is what it says in the preamble, but I can explain this order. This order came into being after we lost our positions to the army of Republika Srpska in the territory of Travnik municipality. This is not an appointment, a permanent appointment. The commander of the sector will remain that for 10 or 15 days until the defence line is established, because you see that the commander is from Kiseljak, an officer is from Busovaca that Zivko is from Zenica, that Mario Cerkez is from Vitez; these were commanders of brigades or municipal headquarters, it depended, being appointed as sector commanders. Which means we used all available forces in order to successfully organise and stop the advance of the Bosnian Serb army. This is operative use, so, these commanders, in addition to their duties as brigade commanders, at the same time were sector commanders. And this lasted for a month or a month-and-a-half. So this is operative use of forces, this exists in military terminology.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, in order to get operative use of forces, did Blaskic need municipal approval, or not?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: In this specific situation the danger was threatening of the Bosnian Serb army entering Travnik. So, we exerted the utmost efforts, together with the BH army, to stop their advance and we succeeded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That wasn't my question. My question was whether or not he needed municipal authority to issue this order on the sector commanders. That was my question.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: When brigade commanders are engaged as sector commanders, then it was up to the commander to assess the situation in the area within the zone of responsibility of a particular brigade, and he would choose the most suitable person. So, in this case he did not need to ask for approval for an already appointed brigade commander to become a sector commander for a month, a month-and-a-half, or for 20 days, as the situation on the battle front.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you would agree with me, Brigadier, that there are some situations, according to your testimony, where Blaskic would need municipal authority, but there are other situations, such as reflected in this exhibit, 456/64, where he does not need municipal authority; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: This order and this example is unique, there are no multiple examples of this kind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This order of appointment and dismissal is unique, is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it is the only one of its kind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's just go through the rest of these very quickly and we'll explore that subject in one moment. Let's turn our attention to the balance of these documents and we have 456/65.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I just want to ask the witness, Brigadier, did you know about this order or you have just discovered it now when the Prosecutor submitted it to you?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I knew of this order. I remember its text because I was involved in the organisation of defence in these sectors. I, at that time, had a different task and a different role and this is why I remember this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Except that you were very categorical when you answered me that General Blaskic could never dismiss without the consent of the other municipal Commanders. You never mentioned there were exceptions.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honour, General Blaskic could never dismiss a Brigade Commander, but if he wanted to appoint 20 persons to help out on a certain task, he did not need any approval, otherwise we wouldn't have been able to function at all the way we did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, let's go back to the exhibit we were just going to discuss again 546/65, an order on the 9th of January, 1993. And in this order, Blaskic calls on the various articles in the Narodni List or the official gazette as would be translated in English and he says: "Pursuant to Article 29, Item 7, Article 30, Item 2, Article 31, Article 34, Item 2 on the decree on armed forces of the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna, and the authorisation issued by the main staff of the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna, Operation Zone 39692 of the 27th" -- excuse me -- "27th of June, 1992, issued an order. Ivica Bagaric from Travnik is appointed chief of the Travnik Brigade, anti-aircraft defence with headquarters in Travnik." Again, another order appointing someone chief of the Travnik Brigade. In this order, did Blaskic have to get the municipal authority?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Just a moment. Just a moment, please. This is the chief -- sorry, my translation was that it was a Brigade Commander. No, he was an expert within the command, a person who is involved in the air defences, so this is within the command structure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, let's clarify the translation and I am reading No. 1 and we should get this clear before I explore this question. It says, "Ivica Bagaric from Travnik is appointed chief of the Travnik Brigade anti-aircraft defence with headquarters in Travnik."

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, with headquarters in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now my question for you is, did Blaskic need the municipal authority approval to appoint Mr. Ivica Bagaric to that position?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: With respect to the officers in the Brigade commands, then the Operative Zone Commander had to do it in agreement with the Brigade Commander. So in order for Mr. Ivica Bagaric to be appointed to this duty, Mr. Blaskic had to reach an agreement with his Brigade Commander on this appointment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, that's not my question. My question is: Did Blaskic need the approval of the municipal authorities to appoint Ivica Bagaric to this particular position as chief of the Travnik Brigade anti-aircraft defence? Did he need the municipal authority approval, or did he not?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I know for officers in the Brigade commands, no approval of the municipal authorities was needed. But the Brigade Commanders' approval was needed. That was the reality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, Brigadier, we have another situation on the appointment of Commanders where Blaskic did not need municipal authority approval in order to appoint somebody; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is not the situation because the military Commanders are the following officers: The commander of squad, platoon, company, battalion and so forth. All other officers are just chiefs of departments. They do not have a command authority and role. So the chief of anti-aircraft defence is an expert position. I was the chief of the operations and training, so I did not have a command role. It was an expert role. So the command position is just command responsibility, be it at a level of squad, platoon, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So again, Brigadier, the bottom line is that he did not need municipal authority approval to appoint Mr. Bagaric to this position? It's a simple question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: He has answered the question, Mr. President. How long is he going to spend on this? It's an anti-aircraft expert position. This man was not a Brigade Commander, not a squad Commander, not a platoon Commander, etc, etc.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let him answer the question yes or no and we'll move on.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could we ask the Judge to turn the microphone on, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman, you have to realise that the witness does not answer the questions directly. For several times now -- please let me speak. You spoke, I listened to you. In fact, I think we're going to stop the question and the Tribunal will make its evaluation. But I wanted to tell you that several times now, the witness answered the questions indirectly. He starts with a long introduction, which, in fact, means that after several moments, the Judges are taken from one subject to another. The witness does not recognise a certain kind of contradiction within his own words, which is what Judge Riad initially brought out. Of course I am going to stop because -- I was going to stop him, but I ask you to keep your calm, Mr. Hayman, because many things are happening here also have to do with the way the witness is answering. The questions are simple in respect of those questions and each time we seem to drift away to an exception, to another exception. That's what I wanted to say. Did you wish to make a comment? I'll give you the floor. I really wanted to share my opinion with you. Mr. Nobilo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Of course the Defence is trying to assist in this proceedings so that it would go as smoothly as possible. But we have problems in terminology. My colleague is confusing certain terms and this is why we have the impression that our witness is not clear. When it was said that Blaskic could not appoint Commanders without the approval of the municipal authorities, this is what my witness is answering to, that it was just a Commander and he could not. The same when we have officers in a field and we have as yet a different category, so there are three different categories here that we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I suggest that Mr. Kehoe ask his questions category by category again. The Brigadier will answer only in a direct fashion very briefly and then the Judges will evaluate because I think that they have received enough information. The Judges will read the orders, the transcripts, the witness' answers and the Prosecutor's questions. All right, Mr. Kehoe, for the last time, would you ask the questions if you have several of them, ask them. The type of command by type of command, if you like. The witness will answer very directly and very succinctly and then the Judges will make their evaluations with the documents that they have and then we're going to move to another subject because it's going to be almost one hour now that we spent -- actually, more than one hour on this subject and especially since we began with it yesterday. Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well the question I have on this document regarding Mr. Bagaric, 456/65 is; did Blaskic, or did he not, need the approval of the municipal authorities to appoint Mr. Bagaric to this position?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: For the appointment up to this position, that is the position of the chief of the anti-aircraft defence, Commander Blaskic did not approval of the municipal authorities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Bagaric have individuals under his command once he received this appointment?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Commander Bagaric did not have any personnel under his command in this duty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Commander Bagaric became chief of the anti-aircraft defence, but he had nobody under him as the chief; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I know, he did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he was working by himself?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I would need to recall the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: It's a direct question. Brigadier, when the Chief Bagaric was the chief of the anti-aircraft defence headquarters, you're saying he had no soldiers under his order, is that what you're saying? That's what you had just said, he had no soldiers under his order because that's going to be put into the record.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he did not have subordinates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's turn to 456/66, Brigadier. Now 456/66, Brigadier, is an order of Blaskic of the 26th of January, 1993, and nomination and an appointment. He talks about due to the current changes in the situation -- we'll go to the order 1: "I nominate and appointment Mr. Milenko Aravpovic as the company Commander of the 1st battalion. And Mr. Pero -- and pardon my pronunciation Drljepan -- is appointed as company logistics officer as well as deputy commander and the former Commander is relieved by this order." And this goes to the Brigade in Busovaca, the Nikola Subic-Zrinski Brigade. Now, with regard to these particular appointments, did Blaskic need the approval of the municipal authorities to appoint and dismiss this personnel?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I cannot answer this question with a simple yes or no, I need to clarify it. When I spoke about the appointment of company Commanders, which are the local units, I explained what the procedure was. This was the procedure: A company Commander would be nominated at a local level in the village or local commune. This nomination would reach the Brigade Commander and then he would forward it to the Operative Zone Commander and this is how this company Commander would have been appointed. It would have come through up to the Operative Zone Commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Do you agree that nothing in this order alludes to this procedure? There is nothing in this order which refers to that type of procedure, do you agree with what I have just said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. President, in no order which we have reviewed is this procedure transparent. I am just talking about the practice. This is the procedure that was followed and Mr. Blaskic was trying to organise the army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The time we were working on documents, you also had documents during direct examination, do you have an additional question about that, Mr. Kehoe?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question by way of clarification is, Brigadier, so your answer is no, that the municipal authorities had no veto decision or veto power over this decision; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: The municipal authorities did not have a veto authority, but they had to get approval from the local commune.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. But it's not in the document. We would have thought that would have been in the document. That has happened on such and such a date, having consulted the representatives of the municipality, you agree that that is not there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: It's possible that the Defence counsel will bring the written proof of that type of procedure that must have been established at staff headquarters. I suppose one party must have acted pursuant to certain type of procedures. But for the time being, we're noting that no reference is made in this order to any type of consultations. Would you please continue Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's go to the last document in this series which is 456/57.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, again, Brigadier, this is an order signed by the accused, Colonel Blaskic, is it not?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's dated the 30th of March, 1993. And Blaskic --

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me, I didn't mean to interrupt there. I'm sorry. This should be 67, Judge. The transcript reads 456/57, it should be 456/67. Is it this document? That's the document. That's the document on the ELMO. Thank you. Now on this document, again Blaskic calls upon his powers in Article 31 and has delegated authority and he actually appoints Mr. Malbasic and takes him from the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade and transfers him to the Bobovac Brigade in Vares. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I do see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, how far away is the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade from the Bobovac Brigade in Vares?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: The Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade was in Novi Travnik and the Bobovac Brigade was in Travnik. Mr. Bobovac was born and lived in Vares with his family.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, again, with regard to Mr. Bobovac, did the municipal authorities have to approve his appointment to the chief of the artillery Brigade -- excuse me, to the chief of the headquarters in the Bobovac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: The municipal authorities did not need to provide approval for the chief staff of the Bobovac Brigade because this was again not a command position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about the position on No. 2 for the chief intelligence in the Bobovac Brigade, Mr. Mijocevic? Did the municipal authorities have to approve that?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, they did not. This is another duty in the command and it is not a command responsibility or duty, it is an expert position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would your explanation be the same with regard to Position No. 3 in the anti-aircraft defence regarding Mr. Jorgic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it is the same. It's another expert position, and not a command position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if we could just go back with, -- Mr. Usher, if I could give the witness again Exhibit 456/64, which is the order of 20 November 1992. Now, turning our attention back to 456/64, you just stated in the transcript that this order is unique. There are no multiple examples of this kind. I think I quoted you correctly from the transcript concerning this. The transcript will reflect it, but I think that's your quote.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, the witness said that there are no other orders of this kind. That is the only type of this type.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Continue, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also noted that there were no orders of Blaskic dismissing Brigade Commanders without the approval of the municipal authorities. Isn't that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, the Commander, General Blaskic, could not dismiss a Brigade Commander without the approval of municipal authorities. He could have sent an order, but I know that in practice such orders were not carried out. I know an example of that kind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let's talk about that. Let's go to Exhibit 456/22. This is also a Defence exhibit, counsel. I am not sure, but if we could -- I know it's in 456/22. Now this is a battle order that, I think, was discussed. I know it was discussed during your direct examination with Mr. Nobilo. It is a battle order signed by the accused and authorised by the accused. I am not positive that is his signature, but you authenticated this document in your direct. Nevertheless, it's dated the 17th of April, 1993, at 23.45 hours. Do you remember this order, Brigadier?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, I do remember this order. The text of the order was written by me upon orders from General Blaskic, and I signed it upon his authority.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this battle order gives instructions to the Ban Jelacic Brigade and it -- and turn to number three, it gives particular instructions to Fojnica; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It says, "To Fojnica, must secure your left flank and launch an attack on Dusina or break through to Sebesic"?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that is what it says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let me give you another order and this is a new document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is 487, 487A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Again, Mr. President, these will all be translated into French, we just don't have them at this point through translation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Brigadier, this is yet another order written on the 18th of April, 1993, at 01.40 hours that was written by you, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: According to the initials and the text of this order, I do remember writing it upon permission from General Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It goes to the Commander of the Fojnica HVO battalion, does it not? That's the instructions to it?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the Commander of the HVO battalion in Fojnica?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: I remember the sir name, Mr. Tuka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: His first name was Stjepan Tuka, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think it was Stjepan, I am quite sure it was Tuka, Stjepan Tuka, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now tell us about this, Brigadier, this was a particular order for the Fojnica battalion to support the Ban Jelacic Brigade on the Ban Jelacic's Brigade left flank; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: From the assignment defined here, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Stjepan Tuka refused to comply with this order, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That caused significant problems in the Central Bosnia Operative Zone headquarters, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it caused problems because at the time the document was written on the 18th of April, there were very fierce battles in Busovaca, Vitez and Kiseljak and that was the reason why that order was addressed to the Commander in Fojnica, to link forces so as to defend the territories of Busovaca, Vitez and Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, the Commander, Tuka, insubordination was very well known within the headquarters, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. The commander of this battalion refused to carry out the order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In a time of war, that is a significant matter; isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the situation we were in, it is a very, very bad thing that he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when this order was issued, there was no fighting going on in Fojnica, was there?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, there were no battles in Fojnica, but assistance was coming to the BH army forces, who were waging the war in Busovaca, was coming through there, and there was a threat of Busovaca, Vitez and Kiseljak falling.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The assignment given to Tuka and his battalion, in part, was to secure the village of Dusina?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes, to secure the village of Dusina, and to advance towards Busovaca stables and link up with forces defending Sebesic. I can show this area to you on the model.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to clarify the point, Brigadier, the Dusina that is reflected in your order to commander Tuka is not the Dusina that is in the Busovaca municipality, lest the record should confuse the two; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Dusina is a village in the territory of the municipality of Fojnica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, after this order and Tuka's refusal to comply, -- let me turn to the next document, Mr. Usher -- you issued another order or drafted another order for Colonel Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is 488, 488A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, Brigadier, in the lower left-hand corner are your initials; are they not?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember the text of this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is sent in what fashion?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: It should have been sent by packet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you would agree with me, Brigadier, that the order sent on 0140 hours that we talked about, as well as this order sent on the 19th at 1800 hours, was sent by packet, and they deal with the combat plans for the Fojnica battalion; don't they?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: The order that we have here is a warning to the commander of the Fojnica battalion that he has to comply with the orders that he receives from his superior command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, suffice it to say that you were giving combat orders over the packet system where you specifically told the Fojnica battalion where to deploy the HVO troops; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the absolutely impossible situation that we were in at that time, when the situation on the battle front was so grave, we sent only the minimum amount of information by packet that we had to send to the unit commander for him to be able to carry out his assignment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The bottom line, again Brigadier, is that in the order that we were talking about, you sent over the packet system an order for Tuka to deploy his troops towards Dusina; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: To deploy his forces towards Dusina, and to control the area towards Sebesic, which is at least 20 kilometres away; so there isn't much precision there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Go directly to the question, please, Mr. Kehoe. There is an order that was sent to the Fojnica battalion, we understand that. We are not contesting it. There is the order of 19 April, what connection are you making? What is the argument that you want to bring out in order to allow the witness to answer? I would like to finish up, before we take our break I would like to finish this theme, having appointments and dismissals of officials with or without authorisation; otherwise we're going to stop this and move to another subject. We can go a little bit longer, but not much more.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, with regard to the appointment and dismissal of people, we have a ways to go on that, especially on this particular subject. But before we go on with that, I would like to clarify a series of questions that was set up, asked by Mr. Nobilo, if I may, Mr. President, and then if that is a convenient time for a break.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During questions by Mr. Nobilo you told Mr. Nobilo that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I still haven't quite understood what was the purpose of these two documents 487 and 488. What is the question? I haven't got the question. We were talking about Dusina, whether this was the real or the wrong Dusina. I would like this to be clear. You presented this document, 487, it's an order given to Stjepan Tuka of Fojnica, and then you took out 488. What is the question? Before you respond to Mr. Nobilo, if you don't clarify that, we're not going to understand anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With regard to this document on the 19th of April 1993, that you have before you, Brigadier, another reminder was sent to the commander of the Fojnica battalion, Stjepan Tuka, to comply with the orders issued by the commander of the Ban Jelacic brigade; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tuka refused to comply again with this reminder; didn't he?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, he refused.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did Blaskic do when Tuka refused to comply both with the first order on the 18th to move towards either Sebesic or Dusina, or his refusal to comply with the 19th reminder order? What did Blaskic do?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Because of the seriousness of the situation, we were at the time in Busovaca, Vitez, and Kiseljak, General Blaskic issued an order to dismiss that commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because of the seriousness of the situation, because Blaskic viewed this as serious, he dismissed Tuka; didn't he?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: General Blaskic issued an order on dismissal, and I will explain how it all ended.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Can the witness explain, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're welcome to explain, Brigadier.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, after the commander of the Fojnica battalion failed to carry out the military orders he received from General Blaskic, and because of the seriousness of the situation, General Blaskic wrote an order to dismiss him. The drafting of that order was done upon consultation with political representatives who exerted their influence on political representatives in Fojnica for this dismissal. However, the dismissal didn't take place immediately. As far as I am informed, they held meetings, they had talks about it, whether it should be done or not; and after pressure on the part of top politicians and the leadership of Herceg-Bosna was brought to bear on political officials in Fojnica, only then did the replacement take place, and after this procedure Tuka was dismissed and replaced.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, we will get into that after the break, with the Court's permission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well, we will have a break until 11.40.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please have the accused brought in. (The accused entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Talking about Mr. Tuka and Blaskic's order to dismiss Tuka, let us take a look at 456/52. And before we get to that, if we can give this particular document first, give that to the witness and we will hand out another exhibit, because we will be using them at the same time.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is 489, 489A for the French version and B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: 489, again, Mr. President, has yet to be translated into French and will be so. I take that back, we have accomplished the French translation. I apologise, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You are so used to there not being a French translation, it is becoming an automatic reflex. You see, I actually have a French translation here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The translation section is about to kill us all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us start first with the new exhibit before we move to Blaskic's order, and this is a letter from Stjepan Tuka. Have you seen this letter before?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: I haven't seen this letter from Stjepan Tuka before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise Mr. Tuka's signature?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: I do recognise. No, I do not. I'm sorry -- the interpreter didn't understand it. Was it yes or no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You do not recognise? There was some confusion in the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: I do not recognise Mr. Tuka's signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's just read this letter briefly, and I think it's on the ELMO. The 20th of April, it comes from the Busovaca Nikola Subic-Zrinski Brigade, the 3rd Fojnica Battalion, to the attention of Commander Tihomir Blaskic. "Dear Colonel: I feel obliged to respond to your warning to comply with orders. Two years ago when I took on the obligation to organise to protect the Croatian people in the municipality of Fojnica, I was aware of what I was getting into. I, therefore, always kept in mind the preservation of peace in the region and thereby the lives of the people and their property. "I am prepared to answer for everything I have done so far and accept any punishment, regardless of its gravity; but I want the Croatian people to try me, and not some, 'saviours', of the Croatian people. "I cannot blindly carry out some of the orders which directly introduce war into Fojnica and which have been imposed on us without prior consultation with those of us who best know the situation here. "I know that you get information from Fojnica from people who portray a completely different picture from the real one. I implement the orders which I am able to carry out, and do the best I can to execute orders which are impossible to implement. "Please do not take my response as justification for not implementing some of the orders. I request you to urgently carry out your threat regarding replacement and appoint someone capable of carrying out all orders. "As for the responsibility, I have already mentioned that I am prepared to accept it, as well. However, I am not prepared to bring misery to the people I am responsible for and to answer for that either to my conscience or to the very same people." Now, let us turn our attention to Exhibit 456/52. Do you see that exhibit, Brigadier? If I could put that on the ELMO, 456/52. It is on the ELMO. Okay. This is an order from Blaskic dated 20 April 1993. Do you have that, Brigadier?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: I do, I do, I have it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is sent to the commander of the Nikola Subic-Zrinski Brigade of Busovaca, the commander of the 3rd Fojnica Battalion of the Nikola Subic-Zrinski Brigade in Fojnica. "Command: I hereby dismiss Mr. Stjepan Tuka from the post of commander of the 3rd Battalion of the Nikola Subic-Zrinski Brigade in Busovaca because of his failure to carry out his combat missions and appoint Mr. Drago Simunic from Fojnica in his place. I am authorising Mr. D. Simunic fully with regard to the running and commanding of the 3rd Battalion. The deadline for the execution of this command shall be three hours after its receipt. Every act contrary to this command shall entail criminal responsibility. Mr. Stjepan Tuka, the previous commander of the 3rd Battalion and Mr. Drago Simunic, the new commander of the 3rd Battalion, shall be responsible to me in case of failure of execution of this command." Do you recall this order, Brigadier?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: I do recall that this order was written in this way and sent to the address indicated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It says that Mr. Tuka is dismissed immediately; doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that is what it says, and I said that because of the person's failure to comply with orders, the commander issued this order on his dismissal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us turn to 456/54, which is an order that is written by Blaskic some 25 minutes after the dismissal of Tuka, again, on the 20th of April 1993 at 12.05.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. Kehoe said after Tuka's replacement, but it should be after the order was issued on his replacement.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is an example when the question contains an allegation that is not correct. Mr. Tuka was not replaced for a whole month-and-a-half after the order was issued; so that the question should not contain allegations which simply are not true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The fact of the matter is, the Court will be able to make that determination when we complete the review of the documents that we are about to go through, and whether or not Tuka was replaced, and when he was replaced, and the powers of Colonel Blaskic to dismiss him and replace him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Kehoe knows what the underlying facts are, he has an ethical obligation not to misrepresent or mislead the Court in that regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, the documents will speak for themselves. The documents coming up will dismiss Tuka, clearly will dismiss Tuka, and the Court can cull from the documents and make the factual determinations. This particular document that we are turning to, Exhibit 456/54, is simply written 25 minutes after the dismissal order for Tuka is written. That was the lead in from one document to the next document, when and where and what happened in Fojnica. I leave it to the Court to decide after the review of the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I suggest we not waste any more time, Mr. Kehoe, continue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In exhibit 456/54, after the dismissal order of Tuka was issued, Blaskic puts the 3rd Fojnica Battalion, which was in the Nikola Subic-Zrinski Brigade in Busovaca, and subordinates it to the Ban Jelacic commander in Kiseljak; doesn't he?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, he does. If I can explain the circumstances under which this document was created. This order on subordination of this battalion to the Ban Jelacic Brigade was due to the gravity of the situation and the fact that it was cut off and our inability to directly have contact with them. This is why the commander of the Operative Zone, at the date and time indicated here, issued the order which we have before us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, let us turn to Exhibit 456/53. Mr. Dubuisson, just for clarity sake, in the record, was there a French copy of 456/53?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, I think there should be one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If not, I have copies of that. I am not sure when 456 was introduced into evidence. All the French copies are there, if not, we have them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. Give me the French version, please. In any case, if you read it, it will be interpreted and everyone will understand what's going on. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this Document 456/53 is a document written by Stjepan Tuka to the Ban Jelacic Brigade on the 20th of April of 1993. It says, "Information on the replacement of the 39rd Fojnica battalion Commander. With reference to the strictly confidential order of the Commander of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, 014417/93 of 20 April 1993, regarding the replacement of a current present Commander of the 3rd Fojnica Battalion Commander, Mr. Stjepan Tuka, son of Augustin and the appointment of a new Commander, Dragan Simunic, son of Ante, we hereby inform you of the following: A meeting of the 3rd Battalion Command will be held on 20 April, 1993, at 1600 hours at which the Commander shall be replaced. You will be informed of the results of the meeting in due course." Now my first question, Brigadier is, do you recognise that stamp? And do you recognise the document?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: This document did not arrive at the Central Bosnia Operative Zone command, but I can explain this document, if I may? The Commander of the Fojnica Battalion, which was subordinated to the Ban Jelacic Brigade, and was under the direct orders to work together with him, is reporting on the actions that he is taking with respect to the dismissal on replacement of the Battalion Commander. It refers in the last paragraph to a meeting which shall take place. And then in the end he says, "You will be informed of the results of the meeting in due course." What happened in that meeting was that the replacement did not take place. Mr. President, this is a very good example of how, in practice, the civilian authorities did have influence on the appointments of Commanders and the amount of influence which they had in appointments and dismissals. Mr. Tuka, himself, should not have taken a decision not to carry out the order and we saw from his letter that he knew what the situation was and what they were supposed to do in the territory of their municipality, but the municipal authorities had exercised pressure on him and they supported him in his refusal to carry out the order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We have to find a way out of this, Mr. Kehoe. These are two completely two different interpretations. Either it is the last meeting he attended before he gave his position to his replacement or, as the witness is saying, things happened differently. We have to go forward and see what happens next. All right show the next document, if you will, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is 490, 490A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I won't be categorical on this, but I don't think we have a French copy translation on this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: It doesn't matter, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now you were just discussing, Brigadier, the meeting that took place and is this document a reflection of that meeting that was held on the 20th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Could you please allow me just to read through it because I have not seen it before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Certainly, certainly.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: From the text you can see that the decision was taken as a conclusion of the meeting which was referred to in the previous document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I want a note for the record, Mr. President. We've never been given this document. We've repeatedly made motions for violations of Rule 68. That is the Prosecutor's duty to give us exculpatory information. The Court has never imposed a sanction based on those motions. It is incredible that we have never been given this. I want to say that for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, counsel can argue all he wants whether or not he thinks this is Rule 68 material. I want the Court to make a full decision concerning Tuka and what Blaskic did on Tuka and whether or not the Court considers this particular document exculpatory, but I reject categorically, the statements by counsel concerning any Rule 68 applicability order to this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, Mr. President, here in the HKD Napredak, is the culture association of Croats in Fojnica and they and the unit command are all rejecting and this is the crown document proving that the chain of command was broken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Do you have the exact translation of this document, please? I would like someone to read it and it will be interpreted. I would like to hear all of the nuances that are in this text.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I will read it, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Could we have the original read? And read from the --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Give it to the translators and the translators can read it, that would be fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, I think that's how it should be done. All right, Mr. Nobilo, read it. And as you're reading, I'll get a specific and exact translation of all the details of the document and then we can respond to the comments that were made. Go ahead, Mr. Nobilo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I am reading the header: "Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, Croatian Defence Council, command of the 3rd battalion of the Ban Josip Jelacic Brigade." The reference number I am not going to read. "Date: 20 April 1993. Defence military secret and strictly confidential. It is addressed to the Vitez Central Bosnia Operative Zone command and Ban Josip Jelacic Brigade command in Kiseljak. And the text runs as follows: "With reference to your Order No. 01-4-417/93 of 20 April 1993, the command of the 3rd Fojnica Battalion has reached the following decision: "Your Order No. 01-4-417/93 of 20 April 1993 is being completely rejected due to the entire work being accomplished so far and the complexity of the current situation in the 3rd Fojnica Battalion. The Croatian people of Fojnica support per say. This unanimous decision is supported by the Croatian people of Fojnica." It was signed by 3rd Fojnica Battalion command. That is the first signature. The second, Fojnica HVO, which is the executive body of the municipality. Three, Croatian Democratic Union, which is the political party. Franciscan monastery, that is the church. Napredak. This is the HKD, issues of Croatian Cultural Association called Napredak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nobilo. Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, let's continue through the balance of these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next two documents, if I may hand these out. Now the first document -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The first document -- the first document is 491, 491A for the French version and B for the English and the second is 492, 492A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now the first document, Brigadier, is a statement that came from the Fojnica Municipal Assembly and we'll read it as follows. This is Exhibit 491. "At a meeting held on 20 April 1993, during which the current military and political situation, and the situation in the region of Central Bosnia were discussed, as well as the recent order of the command of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone regarding the replacement of the Commander of the armed forces of the Fojnica HVO, Mr. Stjepan Tuka, we hereby issue the following statement: "In view that Mr. Stjepan Tuka's contribution so far in maintaining peace and a common existence of a Croatian and Muslim peoples, as well as the dignity of his own people, we give full support to Mr. Stjepan Tuka and all those supporting the policy of a legitimate representatives of a Croatian people in Fojnica. We hope that the Croatian people will be at the same level as their political and military leadership, and that with their support, and by recognising the opinion given in this statement, and by understanding the gravity of a current situation they will continue to build the joint life which can only contribute to the well being of both peoples. Signed, President of the Municipal Assembly, President of the Fojnica SDA, Commander of the Fojnica Municipal TO. The Fojnica Islamic Community and chairman of the Preporad KDM." In conjunction with that, we turn to 492, the press release on this meeting. Which reads -- and if we could put that on the ELMO. It is also dated the 20th of April. "Following unpleasant occurrences in the region of Central Bosnia, we raise our voices against any crime perpetrated in the name of an ideology and people against any human being. The living determine and direct history. Despite all those who claim that the Muslim and Croatian people cannot live side by side, we state that according to our life and experience so far, a life together is possible and without such a life there is no future. We warn all those responsible that they will be held immediately responsible before the people in history. If they do not cease this pointless conflict immediately, therefore, we beseech all those who are concerned about our souls not to defend us from ourselves." Again the notations are of the Fojnica Municipal Assembly, the representatives of military units of both people. The Fojnica Franciscan Monastery, the Fojnica Islamic community and two lines that just say, "Fojnica, Fojnica Cultural Association and the Islamic Cultural Association." Now, my first question, Brigadier, is: Did you see these documents and were they forwarded to the headquarters?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did not see these documents, and from the contents of the documents, I see that there are no reference numbers which we would have placed on them if they had arrived at the Operative Zone command, so I cannot say that they have ever arrived there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Blaskic responded to all of this, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: I do not know whether General Blaskic responded to this, but on 20 April, and due to the serious situation and fierce attacks in Busovaca, Vitez, he was involved in those issues and he contacted with the HVO top in order to have his order on the dismissal of Tuka carried out because by that time it had not been carried out yet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let's turn our attention to another new exhibit. Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Is this the same subject?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Same subject, Mr. President. Last document on the subject.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: About Fojnica as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, the last document on the subject, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is 493, 493A for the French version and B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Brigadier, taking a look at this document, does this document reflect the name and the Broj number or the number coming from the Central Bosnia Operative Zone command and that being Commander Blaskic. I refer you to the No. 01-5 -- 5 being for the month of May, 167/93. Does that reflect a number coming from the headquarters of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: In that period that was the way things were registered, so I assume that this was registered with the Operative Zone command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this a document that was sent in the packet communication system?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: By superiors it looks as if has been sent by packet, but I cannot see who is behind it. It may have been produced through photocopying, at least that is the copy I am looking at.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, no doubt. But I am talking about the actual print, it would appear to be the use of the packet communications that other orders going down to the Fojnica command that were used to communicate with the Fojnica Battalion and to Mr. Tuka; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN (Resumed)
utterances.text: Based on the number and appearance of the header, those are the facts which lead me to believe that this document may have been drafted at the Operative Zone command. However, there is no name or signature to see who the actual drafter of the document was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, this document is incomplete. This document is incomplete. Something is missing here. It has the first and last pages, but there is something there. It is not in a logical way. Even if it was received by the packet communication, I think there is a portion of this document missing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, it's true. The actual impression of this photocopy that something was put together here. It is kind as if a collific collage was made. Yes, Mr. Kehoe, two things were put together here, were they not?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, in a private session outside the presence of the Brigadier, we can explain where this document came from, how it came into the possession of the Office of the Prosecutor in order to authenticate this document and we can pull up the original that was provided to the Office of the Prosecutor from the vault should the Chamber so desire. But if we want to talk about some preliminary matters concerning this document, and the folds, etc, we would like to do that in private session outside with the presence of the Brigadier. With all due respect, Brigadier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You're talking about the accused or the witness here?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The witness, Mr. President, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Defence does not dispute the authenticity of this document, but we say that we do not have the integral document. In other words, we recognise it's authenticity, but dispute its completeness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Is it true, there is a part missing?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is what we were provided. If counsel has got the full document that was sent by Blaskic, then he should provide it. This is what we have. Once again, I offer to Mr. President, and Your Honours, I will pull up what the original is in the vault and provide to it the Court for review.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Defence has never seen Exhibits 490, 491, 492 or 493 before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Well, we understood that, Mr. Hayman. You are saying that that falls under Rule 68. But sometimes you've got a very broad interpretation of Rule 68. It's not because a document has been provided and that it contradicts a statement of a witness that it automatically means that it is a document that should have been provided under Rule 68. Therefore, for the time being, I was waiting personally for the end of the sequence and to see whether Mr. Stjepan Tuka was or was not dismissed from his post despite the recriminations expressed by the municipality. I think that is what the discussion is centring around. Mr. Hayman?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I won't belabour the point. I think it would have been profitable, perhaps to show this series of documents to Brigadier Duncan. To some of the other professional western military officers who came in the Prosecutor's case and ask them: Is this how the unity of chain of command is supposed to function? Is this how a Commander is supposed to be able to exercise his powers? Or, rather, is it something else?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: That's the Prosecutor's work, Mr. Hayman. Mr. Hayman, don't do Mr. Kehoe's work. Mr. Kehoe has apparently preferred to submit this to the witness. Let me summarise things, Mr. Hayman, and then I will give the floor back to you. For the time being, what we're talking about is something very, very specific. We have been talking about it since yesterday. We are at a very exact point of knowing whether Colonel Blaskic, who was the Commander of the Operative Zone, had the power to appoint or to dismiss operational Commanders with all nuances that were expressed by the witness and which have been put into the record. Did he have that power? Mr. Kehoe for the past hour has been trying to show to the witness that a specific case, that is the dismissal of Mr. Stjepan Tuka, the accused, who at the time was Colonel Blaskic, did not need and did not have a legal administrative or military need to consult with the political municipal authorities. You are saying the opposite, you are saying, as is the witness, you said that both the Documents 490 and 91 really supported. But you said I didn't want to say anything because I was waiting for the sequence, the end of what was going on here. And then afterwards you could draw any conclusions or arguments you want from this sequence, but I think it's important for the Judges, that is that they should have an idea of the answer to the question and know whether the accused was able to dismiss Mr. Tuka without having the opinion of the municipal local authorities. That's what we're talking about. Now we have to look at the document. You raised a new question when you said that this document is one's whose authenticity we're not contesting, but you thought it was incomplete. And simply reviewing this to say that you are right, it is incomplete, and the Prosecutor admitted that. That's where we are. Let's try to move forward. Mr. Hayman, if you're not satisfied with my summary, although I thought it was clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I think we are speaking past one another. All we are saying with respect to Rule 68 -- -- JUDGE JORDA: I'm sure that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: The Prosecutor has been urging the Court, upon the Court, the position that Colonel Blaskic did not have to consult with political or municipal authorities in the process of replacing commanders. These documents speak for themselves. Not only did he have to consult --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: No, not at all, Mr. Hayman, not at all. It's not because there was a meeting. You want me to answer, I really don't like to, but it's not -- because civilian representatives were there to discuss things that didn't come to agreement, that would automatically mean that in the thesis in the Prosecutor's statement that he didn't have to consult with the authorities. You have to look at administrative and legal and military aspects of consultations. You cannot prevent people from doing that, and that's why deliberately I was waiting for the final document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: For the record, I just, if I could finish, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: For the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Exhibit 490 is signed by civilian and municipal authorities.
